entries.title: Proverbs 25:11
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: word. 15:23; 24:26; Ec 12:10; Isa 50:4 fitly spoken. Heb. spoken upon his wheels. is like.Rather "is like golden apples ({tappuchim,} in Arabic, {tuffach,}) in baskets ({maskeeyoth,} in Arabic, {shakeekat,}) of silver." A word spoken with propriety, opportunely, and suitably to the occasion, is as much in its place, and as conspicuously beautiful, as the golden fruit which appears through the apertures of an exquisitely wrought silver basket.

entries.content: long. 15:1; 16:14; Ge 32:4-21; 1Sa 25:14,24-44; Ec 10:4 the bone.Rather, "a bone;" that is, soft and conciliating language will often accomplish the most difficult things.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:22

entries.content:
For.Not to consume, but to melt him into kindness; a metaphor taken from smelting metalic ores.

the Lord. 2Sa 16:12; Mt 10:13; 1Co 15:18

entries.title: Proverbs 25:23
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
north. Job 37:22 driveth, etc. or, bringeth forth rain; so doth a backbitingtongue an angry countenance. Monconys says, that when travelling on the second of January, 1648, from Tripoli in Syria, between Lebanon and the sea, it rained without ceasing, while the north wind blew directly in his face.

so. 26:20; Ps 15:3; 101:5; Ro 1:30; 2Co 12:20
